html:
The Chiricahua are an Apache people of southeast Arizona, southwest New Mexico and the mountains of northern Sonora and Chihuahua. At the time of European contact they held some 60,000 square kilometres of mountain and desert.

They lived by hunting, gathering and raiding, and from the late 1600s they raided Spanish and then Mexican settlements for horses and cattle. Their leaders of the 1800s are among the most famous Native Americans: Mangas Coloradas, his son-in-law Cochise, Victorio and Geronimo. Cochise made peace with the United States in 1872 and won a reservation in the Chiricahua Mountains, but it was closed after his death. Geronimo's band held out until 1886.

After the surrender the US Army sent the whole people, even those who had served it as scouts, as prisoners of war to Florida, then Alabama, then Fort Sill in Oklahoma. They were freed only in 1913. Some moved to the Mescalero reservation in New Mexico; others stayed at Fort Sill.
